The US on Wednesday proposed a tariff of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, following a months-long investigation into what Washington calls 'structural excess capacity' in 16 major economies. The rate would fall to 17 per cent if New Delhi signs a trade deal with Washington, according to a list released by the office of the US Trade Representative (USTR).
However, in this interview, former US Trade Representative Mark Linscott says U.S. can't expect that India will reduce its manufacturing push, which is something the Trump administration has flagged.
Watch.
